# Codebase Inspection with pygount

Analyze repositories for lines of code, language breakdown, file counts, and code-vs-comment ratios using `pygount`.

## When to Use

- User asks for LOC (lines of code) count
- User wants a language breakdown of a repo
- User asks about codebase size or composition
- User wants code-vs-comment ratios
- General "how big is this repo" questions

## Prerequisites

```bash
pip install --break-system-packages pygount 2>/dev/null || pip install pygount
```

## 1. Basic Summary (Most Common)

Get a full language breakdown with file counts, code lines, and comment lines:

```bash
cd /path/to/repo
pygount --format=summary \
  --folders-to-skip=".git,node_modules,venv,.venv,__pycache__,.cache,dist,build,.next,.tox,.eggs,*.egg-info" \
  .
```

**IMPORTANT:** Always use `--folders-to-skip` to exclude dependency/build directories, otherwise pygount will crawl them and take a very long time or hang.

## 2. Common Folder Exclusions

Adjust based on the project type:

```bash
# Python projects
--folders-to-skip=".git,venv,.venv,__pycache__,.cache,dist,build,.tox,.eggs,.mypy_cache"

# JavaScript/TypeScript projects
--folders-to-skip=".git,node_modules,dist,build,.next,.cache,.turbo,coverage"

# General catch-all
--folders-to-skip=".git,node_modules,venv,.venv,__pycache__,.cache,dist,build,.next,.tox,vendor,third_party"
```

## 3. Filter by Specific Language

```bash
# Only count Python files
pygount --suffix=py --format=summary .

# Only count Python and YAML
pygount --suffix=py,yaml,yml --format=summary .
```

## 4. Detailed File-by-File Output

```bash
# Default format shows per-file breakdown
pygount --folders-to-skip=".git,node_modules,venv" .

# Sort by code lines (pipe through sort)
pygount --folders-to-skip=".git,node_modules,venv" . | sort -t$'\t' -k1 -nr | head -20
```

## 5. Output Formats

```bash
# Summary table (default recommendation)
pygount --format=summary .

# JSON output for programmatic use
pygount --format=json .

# Pipe-friendly: Language, file count, code, docs, empty, string
pygount --format=summary . 2>/dev/null
```

## 6. Interpreting Results

The summary table columns:
- **Language** — detected programming language
- **Files** — number of files of that language
- **Code** — lines of actual code (executable/declarative)
- **Comment** — lines that are comments or documentation
- **%** — percentage of total

Special pseudo-languages:
- `__empty__` — empty files
- `__binary__` — binary files (images, compiled, etc.)
- `__generated__` — auto-generated files (detected heuristically)
- `__duplicate__` — files with identical content
- `__unknown__` — unrecognized file types

## Pitfalls

1. **Always exclude .git, node_modules, venv** — without `--folders-to-skip`, pygount will crawl everything and may take minutes or hang on large dependency trees.
2. **Markdown shows 0 code lines** — pygount classifies all Markdown content as comments, not code. This is expected behavior.
3. **JSON files show low code counts** — pygount may count JSON lines conservatively. For accurate JSON line counts, use `wc -l` directly.
4. **Large monorepos** — for very large repos, consider using `--suffix` to target specific languages rather than scanning everything.

# GitHub Repository Management

Create, clone, fork, configure, and manage GitHub repositories. Each section shows `gh` first, then the `git` + `curl` fallback.

## Prerequisites

- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)

### Setup

```bash
if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
  AUTH="gh"
else
  AUTH="git"
  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    if _hermes_env="${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/.env"; [ -f "$_hermes_env" ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env"; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\n\r')
    elif grep -q "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's|https://[^:]*:\([^@]*\)@.*|\1|')
    fi
  fi
fi

# Get your GitHub username (needed for several operations)
if [ "$AUTH" = "gh" ]; then
  GH_USER=$(gh api user --jq '.login')
else
  GH_USER=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['login'])")
fi
```

If you're inside a repo already:

```bash
REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
```

---

## 1. Cloning Repositories

Cloning is pure `git` — works identically either way:

```bash
# Clone via HTTPS (works with credential helper or token-embedded URL)
git clone https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git

# Clone into a specific directory
git clone https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git ./my-local-dir

# Shallow clone (faster for large repos)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git

# Clone a specific branch
git clone --branch develop https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git

# Clone via SSH (if SSH is configured)
git clone git@github.com:owner/repo-name.git
```

**With gh (shorthand):**

```bash
gh repo clone owner/repo-name
gh repo clone owner/repo-name -- --depth 1
```

## 2. Creating Repositories

**With gh:**

```bash
# Create a public repo and clone it
gh repo create my-new-project --public --clone

# Private, with description and license
gh repo create my-new-project --private --description "A useful tool" --license MIT --clone

# Under an organization
gh repo create my-org/my-new-project --public --clone

# From existing local directory
cd /path/to/existing/project
gh repo create my-project --source . --public --push
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
# Create the remote repo via API
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/user/repos \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-new-project",
    "description": "A useful tool",
    "private": false,
    "auto_init": true,
    "license_template": "mit"
  }'

# Clone it
git clone https://github.com/$GH_USER/my-new-project.git
cd my-new-project

# -- OR -- push an existing local directory to the new repo
cd /path/to/existing/project
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git remote add origin https://github.com/$GH_USER/my-new-project.git
git push -u origin main
```

To create under an organization:

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/orgs/my-org/repos \
  -d '{"name": "my-new-project", "private": false}'
```

### From a Template

**With gh:**

```bash
gh repo create my-new-app --template owner/template-repo --public --clone
```

**With curl:**

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/owner/template-repo/generate \
  -d '{"owner": "'"$GH_USER"'", "name": "my-new-app", "private": false}'
```

## 3. Forking Repositories

**With gh:**

```bash
gh repo fork owner/repo-name --clone
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
# Create the fork via API
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo-name/forks

# Wait a moment for GitHub to create it, then clone
sleep 3
git clone https://github.com/$GH_USER/repo-name.git
cd repo-name

# Add the original repo as "upstream" remote
git remote add upstream https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git
```

### Keeping a Fork in Sync

```bash
# Pure git — works everywhere
git fetch upstream
git checkout main
git merge upstream/main
git push origin main
```

**With gh (shortcut):**

```bash
gh repo sync $GH_USER/repo-name
```

## 4. Repository Information

**With gh:**

```bash
gh repo view owner/repo-name
gh repo list --limit 20
gh search repos "machine learning" --language python --sort stars
```

**With curl:**

```bash
# View repo details
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
r = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(f\"Name: {r['full_name']}\")
print(f\"Description: {r['description']}\")
print(f\"Stars: {r['stargazers_count']}  Forks: {r['forks_count']}\")
print(f\"Default branch: {r['default_branch']}\")
print(f\"Language: {r['language']}\")"

# List your repos
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.github.com/user/repos?per_page=20&sort=updated" \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for r in json.load(sys.stdin):
    vis = 'private' if r['private'] else 'public'
    print(f\"  {r['full_name']:40}  {vis:8}  {r.get('language', ''):10}  ★{r['stargazers_count']}\")"

# Search repos
curl -s \
  "https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=machine+learning+language:python&sort=stars&per_page=10" \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for r in json.load(sys.stdin)['items']:
    print(f\"  {r['full_name']:40}  ★{r['stargazers_count']:6}  {r['description'][:60] if r['description'] else ''}\")"
```

## 5. Repository Settings

**With gh:**

```bash
gh repo edit --description "Updated description" --visibility public
gh repo edit --enable-wiki=false --enable-issues=true
gh repo edit --default-branch main
gh repo edit --add-topic "machine-learning,python"
gh repo edit --enable-auto-merge
```

**With curl:**

```bash
curl -s -X PATCH \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO \
  -d '{
    "description": "Updated description",
    "has_wiki": false,
    "has_issues": true,
    "allow_auto_merge": true
  }'

# Update topics
curl -s -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.mercy-preview+json" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/topics \
  -d '{"names": ["machine-learning", "python", "automation"]}'
```

## 6. Branch Protection

```bash
# View current protection
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/branches/main/protection

# Set up branch protection
curl -s -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/branches/main/protection \
  -d '{
    "required_status_checks": {
      "strict": true,
      "contexts": ["ci/test", "ci/lint"]
    },
    "enforce_admins": false,
    "required_pull_request_reviews": {
      "required_approving_review_count": 1
    },
    "restrictions": null
  }'
```

## 7. Secrets Management (GitHub Actions)

**With gh:**

```bash
gh secret set API_KEY --body "your-secret-value"
gh secret set SSH_KEY < ~/.ssh/id_rsa
gh secret list
gh secret delete API_KEY
```

**With curl:**

Secrets require encryption with the repo's public key — more involved via API:

```bash
# Get the repo's public key for encrypting secrets
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/secrets/public-key

# Encrypt and set (requires Python with PyNaCl)
python3 -c "
from base64 import b64encode
from nacl import encoding, public
import json, sys

# Get the public key
key_id = '<key_id_from_above>'
public_key = '<base64_key_from_above>'

# Encrypt
sealed = public.SealedBox(
    public.PublicKey(public_key.encode('utf-8'), encoding.Base64Encoder)
).encrypt('your-secret-value'.encode('utf-8'))
print(json.dumps({
    'encrypted_value': b64encode(sealed).decode('utf-8'),
    'key_id': key_id
}))"

# Then PUT the encrypted secret
curl -s -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/secrets/API_KEY \
  -d '<output from python script above>'

# List secrets (names only, values hidden)
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/secrets \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for s in json.load(sys.stdin)['secrets']:
    print(f\"  {s['name']:30}  updated: {s['updated_at']}\")"
```

Note: For secrets, `gh secret set` is dramatically simpler. If setting secrets is needed and `gh` isn't available, recommend installing it for just that operation.

## 8. Releases

**With gh:**

```bash
gh release create v1.0.0 --title "v1.0.0" --generate-notes
gh release create v2.0.0-rc1 --draft --prerelease --generate-notes
gh release create v1.0.0 ./dist/binary --title "v1.0.0" --notes "Release notes"
gh release list
gh release download v1.0.0 --dir ./downloads
```

**With curl:**

```bash
# Create a release
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases \
  -d '{
    "tag_name": "v1.0.0",
    "name": "v1.0.0",
    "body": "## Changelog\n- Feature A\n- Bug fix B",
    "draft": false,
    "prerelease": false,
    "generate_release_notes": true
  }'

# List releases
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for r in json.load(sys.stdin):
    tag = r.get('tag_name', 'no tag')
    print(f\"  {tag:15}  {r['name']:30}  {'draft' if r['draft'] else 'published'}\")"

# Upload a release asset (binary file)
RELEASE_ID=<id_from_create_response>
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  "https://uploads.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases/$RELEASE_ID/assets?name=binary-amd64" \
  --data-binary @./dist/binary-amd64
```

## 9. GitHub Actions Workflows

**With gh:**

```bash
gh workflow list
gh run list --limit 10
gh run view <RUN_ID>
gh run view <RUN_ID> --log-failed
gh run rerun <RUN_ID>
gh run rerun <RUN_ID> --failed
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main
gh workflow run deploy.yml -f environment=staging
```

**With curl:**

```bash
# List workflows
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/workflows \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for w in json.load(sys.stdin)['workflows']:
    print(f\"  {w['id']:10}  {w['name']:30}  {w['state']}\")"

# List recent runs
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs?per_page=10" \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for r in json.load(sys.stdin)['workflow_runs']:
    print(f\"  Run {r['id']}  {r['name']:30}  {r['conclusion'] or r['status']}\")"

# Download failed run logs
RUN_ID=<run_id>
curl -s -L \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/logs \
  -o /tmp/ci-logs.zip
cd /tmp && unzip -o ci-logs.zip -d ci-logs

# Re-run a failed workflow
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/rerun

# Re-run only failed jobs
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/rerun-failed-jobs

# Trigger a workflow manually (workflow_dispatch)
WORKFLOW_ID=<workflow_id_or_filename>
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/dispatches \
  -d '{"ref": "main", "inputs": {"environment": "staging"}}'
```

## 10. Gists

**With gh:**

```bash
gh gist create script.py --public --desc "Useful script"
gh gist list
```

**With curl:**

```bash
# Create a gist
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/gists \
  -d '{
    "description": "Useful script",
    "public": true,
    "files": {
      "script.py": {"content": "print(\"hello\")"}
    }
  }'

# List your gists
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/gists \
  | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for g in json.load(sys.stdin):
    files = ', '.join(g['files'].keys())
    print(f\"  {g['id']}  {g['description'] or '(no desc)':40}  {files}\")"
```

## Quick Reference Table

| Action | gh | git + curl |
|--------|-----|-----------|
| Clone | `gh repo clone o/r` | `git clone https://github.com/o/r.git` |
| Create repo | `gh repo create name --public` | `curl POST /user/repos` |
| Fork | `gh repo fork o/r --clone` | `curl POST /repos/o/r/forks` + `git clone` |
| Repo info | `gh repo view o/r` | `curl GET /repos/o/r` |
| Edit settings | `gh repo edit --...` | `curl PATCH /repos/o/r` |

messages.content:
{"content": "1|# Autoframe
2|
3|Autoframe is a QA automation framework with an AI assistant built in. You clone it, tell the AI about your app, and it writes Playwright tests with you, in a structure that holds up as your product grows.
4|
5|It covers the three kinds of testing most teams need, in one place:
6|
7|- **End-to-end**: does the app work the way a user experiences it? Can they log in, add to cart, check out?
8|- **API**: do the backend endpoints respond correctly, including when given bad input?
9|- **Load**: does the app stay up when a hundred people use it at once?
10|
11|Most teams run three different tools for this. Here it's one framework, one set of conventions, one AI that understands all of it.
12|
13|## Who this is for
14|
15|**QA engineers.** If you've been testing manually and want to start automating, this is the lowest-friction path I know of. You describe what to test in plain English and the AI writes the code following professional patterns. When you don't understand something, type `/explain` and it walks you through the file like a patient mentor. If you already automate, the value is speed: Page Objects, specs, fixtures and CI generated in minutes instead of assembled by hand.
16|
17|**Developers.** The stack is Playwright and TypeScript, strict mode, Page Object Model, custom fixtures, parallel runs across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The part you'll actually care about: `/review-spec` reviews your tests the way a senior QA would, and it catches the mistake most of us make, which is testing the implementation instead of the behavior.
18|
19|**PMs and founders.** You don't need to touch the code. `/report` turns the test suite into a plain-English summary you can paste into a board update: what's verified, what's not yet covered, what the risk is. `/load-k6` answers the launch-week question, "will it hold up under traffic?", with hard numbers instead of hope.
20|
21|## What the tests look like
22|
23|Test names are written so anyone on the team can read a failure and know what broke:
24|
25|```typescript
26|test.describe('Login', () => {
27|  test('a standard user can sign in and reach the products page', ...);
28|  test('a wrong password is rejected with an error message', ...);
29|  test('submitting an empty form asks the user for a username', ...);
30|});
31|```
32|
33|Every feature gets happy path, negative and edge cases. Failures come with screenshots, videos and a shareable HTML report (Allure). Tests also run automatically on every push via GitHub Actions.
34|
35|## Proven on real apps
36|
37|Before release, Autoframe was validated end to end against two public demo apps:
38|
39|- **[saucedemo.com](https://www.saucedemo.com)**: login, inventory and cart suites, 10 E2E tests running green across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
40|- **[automationexercise.com](https://automationexercise.com)**: products and auth API suites, 8 tests including a full create, verify and delete account lifecycle using generated test data.
41|
42|That comes to 38 passing tests across three browsers and a live API. Dogfooding the AI commands during validation also surfaced three real framework bugs: a config issue that leaked API tests into browser runs, a command name collision, and a skill format mismatch. All three were fixed before shipping. The k6 load path was verified end to end too, including confirming that a breached performance threshold correctly fails the build.
43|
44|## Getting started
45|
46|You'll need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) and [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), the AI assistant that powers the commands.
47|
48|**1. Get the code**
49|
50|```bash
51|git clone https://github.com/kint4/autoframe.git my-tests
52|cd my-tests
53|```
54|
55|**2. Install the tooling** (takes a couple of minutes)
56|
57|```bash
58|npm install
59|npx playwright install
60|```
61|
62|**3. Let the AI set everything up**
63|
64|Open the folder in Claude Code and type:
65|
66|```
67|/setup
68|```
69|
70|It asks a few questions: your app's address, how users log in, what to test first. Then it builds a working suite around your answers and runs it against your real app.
71|
72|**4. Run your tests**
73|
74|```bash
75|npm test        # run everything
76|npm run report  # open a visual report you can share
77|```
78|
79|## The commands
80|
81|The ones you'll use most days:
82|
83|| Command | What it does |
84||---|---|
85|| `/setup` | Sets up the framework for your app. Start here. |
86|| `/new-spec` | Writes tests for a feature: happy path, errors, edge cases |
87|| `/tc-to-spec` | Paste requirements or a Notion/Jira link, get runnable tests |
88|| `/explain` | Explains any file in plain language |
89|| `/report` | Coverage summary written for non-technical readers |
90|
91|The rest, when you need them:
92|
93|| Command | What it does |
94||---|---|
95|| `/new-page` | Creates a Page Object, a reusable map of one page of your app |
96|| `/coverage-map` | Shows what's tested, what's missing, what's redundant |
97|| `/flake-check` | Diagnoses tests that fail randomly |
98|| `/bug-from-failure` | Turns a failing test into a ready-to-file bug report |
99|| `/review-spec` | Reviews your tests like a senior QA would |
100|| `/refactor` | Restructures messy existing tests into this framework's style |
101|| `/new-api-spec` | Writes tests for a backend API endpoint |
102|| `/api-coverage` | Shows which API endpoints are tested and which aren't |
103|| `/load-k6` | Creates a load test for a traffic scenario you describe |
104|
105|## Using a different AI tool?
106|
107|The framework itself (Playwright, TypeScript, k6, the conventions and CI) works with any AI assistant, or none at all. You can clone it and write tests by hand.
108|
109|The slash commands above are wired for Claude Code today: they live in `.claude/skills/` and the conventions live in `CLAUDE.md`, both of which Claude Code loads automatically. Other tools won't pick them up on their own. If you use Codex, Cursor, or another LLM, you can still point it at `CLAUDE.md` and the skill files manually, since they are just structured instructions. Better yet, fork the repo and port that layer to your tool's format (for example an `AGENTS.md` for Codex, or `.cursor/rules` for Cursor). Pull requests that add support for other tools are very welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how.
110|
111|## Where things live
112|
113|The AI puts files in the right place for you, but here's the map:
114|
115|```
116|tests/e2e/         the tests themselves, organized by feature
117|tests/api/         backend API tests
118|pages/             Page Objects that tests reuse
119|fixtures/          wiring that injects Page Objects into tests
120|data/              realistic fake test data (Faker)
121|performance/load/  k6 load test scripts
122|.github/workflows/ CI pipelines that run on every push
123|```
124|
125|## Good to know
126|
127|- Your app's URL and test credentials live in a `.env` file on your machine. It is never committed. `/setup` sets it up for you.
128|- Stuck on any file? `/explain` it. That's what it's for.
129|- The full design rationale is in [AUTOFRAME.md](AUTOFRAME.md), and the conventions the AI follows are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).
130|
131|---
132|
133|*Autoframe, an AI-native QA automation framework. github.com/kint4/autoframe*

{"content": "1|# Autoframe
2|
3|> AI-native QA automation framework that bootstraps a production-grade Playwright suite for any web product in minutes.
4|
5|---
6|
7|## What is Autoframe?
8|
9|Autoframe is an opinionated, AI-native QA automation framework built on Playwright + TypeScript. It combines a production-ready framework structure with AI-powered skills that handle the tedious parts of automation: scaffolding Page Objects, generating specs from requirements, diagnosing flaky tests, mapping coverage, and running load tests.
10|
11|The goal is simple: clone the repo, run `/setup`, and have a real, maintainable, scaling test suite in 30 minutes — not 3 days.
12|
13|Autoframe is not a template. It is a framework factory. The AI skills grow your suite as your product evolves, so automation stays current instead of going stale.
14|
15|---
16|
17|## The Problem
18|
19|Most QA automation frameworks leave too much to the engineer:
20|
21|- Structure decisions that rot in 6 months
22|- Boilerplate that takes days to wire up
23|- No guidance on what to automate first
24|- Tests that go stale as the product changes
25|- No connection between requirements and test coverage
26|- Performance and load testing living in completely separate tools
27|
28|Autoframe solves all of these in one place.
29|
30|---
31|
32|## Stack
33|
34|| Tool | Purpose |
35||---|---|
36|| Playwright | Functional E2E + API testing |
37|| TypeScript | Type safety across the entire suite |
38|| k6 | Load testing |
39|| Allure Report | Test reporting |
40|| GitHub Actions | CI/CD |
41|| Faker.js | Test data generation |
42|
43|**Autoframe is opinionated about its stack.** It does not support Jest, Cypress, or other test runners. Playwright + TypeScript, full stop. This is intentional — opinionated frameworks are easier to build, maintain, document, and contribute to.
44|
45|---
46|
47|## Four Personas
48|
49|### Persona 1: Manual QA → First Automation Project
50|QA engineers who have been testing manually for years and need to start automating. They know what to test but not how to structure it in code. They need hand-holding, not just scaffolding.
51|
52|**Their biggest fear:** "I don't know where to start."
53|**What Autoframe gives them:** A working framework on day one, with `/explain` to teach them the patterns behind the generated code.
54|
55|### Persona 2: QA Automation Engineer Accelerating Development
56|Experienced automation engineers who already know Playwright but waste too much time on boilerplate, structure decisions, and framework maintenance.
57|
58|**Their biggest pain:** "I spend more time on framework setup than writing actual tests."
59|**What Autoframe gives them:** 10x speed on every repetitive task, from POM generation to coverage reporting.
60|
61|### Persona 3: Developer Who Wants Automation
62|Fullstack or backend developers who need to add E2E automation but don't have QA experience. They understand code deeply but don't know QA patterns or what to test.
63|
64|**Their biggest gap:** "I write tests that test implementation, not behavior."
65|**What Autoframe gives them:** `/review-spec` that critiques their tests from a QA perspective, and structure that prevents common developer testing mistakes.
66|
67|### Persona 4: Business or Product Wanting MVP Test Automation
68|Non-technical or semi-technical stakeholders who need coverage proof, load testing validation, or a quick automation foundation for a new product.
69|
70|**Their biggest need:** "Prove to me the app works and can handle traffic."
71|**What Autoframe gives them:** `/report` for stakeholder-friendly coverage summaries and `/load-k6` for load testing validation before releases.
72|
73|---
74|
75|## Folder Structure
76|
77|Feature-based structure that scales with the product:
78|
79|```
80|autoframe/
81|├── tests/
82|│   ├── e2e/
83|│   │   ├── auth/
84|│   │   ├── checkout/
85|│   │   └── dashboard/
86|│   └── api/
87|│       ├── auth/
88|│       └── checkout/
89|├── performance/
90|│   └── load/               ← k6 scripts
91|├── pages/
92|│   ├── auth/
93|│   ├── checkout/
94|│   └── dashboard/
95|├── fixtures/
96|├── data/
97|│   ├── factories/          ← Faker.js typed factories
98|│   └── seeds/
99|├── utils/
100|│   ├── helpers.ts
101|│   └── constants.ts
102|├── .claude/
103|│   └── skills/             ← 14 AI skill markdown files
104|├── .github/
105|│   └── workflows/
106|│       ├── e2e.yml
107|│       ├── api.yml
108|│       └── load.yml
109|├── AUTOFRAME.md            ← this file
110|├── CLAUDE.md               ← instructions for Claude (root level)
111|├── README.md               ← public facing documentation
112|├── .env.example            ← environment variable template
113|├── .gitignore
114|├── package.json
115|├── playwright.config.ts
116|└── tsconfig.json
117|```
118|
119|**Why feature-based?**
120|- Easy to find tests by feature, mirrors how PMs and devs think
121|- `/coverage-map` can report coverage per feature naturally
122|- Scales cleanly as the product grows
123|- New contributors understand the structure immediately
124|
125|---
126|
127|## 14 Skills
128|
129|### Setup
130|| Skill | Description |
131||---|---|
132|| `/setup` | Bootstraps the entire framework for a specific product. Asks app URL, auth type, stack, CI platform. Outputs a fully wired, ready-to-run project. Includes a simple mode for non-technical users. |
133|
134|### Functional E2E
135|| Skill | Description |
136||---|---|
137|| `/new-page` | Generates a typed Page Object for a given URL, following Autoframe's POM conventions. |
138|| `/new-spec` | Generates a spec file for a given feature or page. Happy path, negative cases, and edge cases pre-written. |
139|| `/tc-to-spec` | Takes requirements (pasted text, Notion URL, Jira ticket, or any connector) and generates a runnable spec file. |
140|| `/flake-check` | Analyzes failing or unstable tests, diagnoses flaky selectors vs timing issues vs real bugs. |
141|| `/coverage-map` | Reads all spec files, maps them against requirements, shows what is covered, missing, and redundant. |
142|| `/bug-from-failure` | Turns a test failure into a structured bug report with repro steps, severity, environment, expected vs actual. |
143|| `/explain` | Explains any generated file in plain language. Teaches the pattern behind the code, not just the output. |
144|| `/refactor` | Takes existing messy Playwright tests and restructures them to follow Autoframe conventions. |
145|| `/review-spec` | Reviews a spec file from a QA perspective. Flags weak assertions, missing coverage, implementation-focused tests. |
146|| `/report` | Generates a non-technical test coverage summary for stakeholders. Ready to share with PMs, CTOs, or boards. |
147|
148|### API
149|| Skill | Description |
150||---|---|
151|| `/new-api-spec` | Generates an API test file for a given endpoint. Covers GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, auth headers, and response schema validation. |
152|| `/api-coverage` | Maps API endpoints against existing API tests. Shows what is tested, what is missing. |
153|
154|### Load
155|| Skill | Description |
156||---|---|
157|| `/load-k6` | Generates a k6 load test script for a described scenario. Defines stages, thresholds, and outputs a readable report. |
158|
159|---
160|
161|## Input Strategy
162|
163|Autoframe does not care where requirements come from. It accepts:
164|
165|- **Plain text** — paste requirements directly, no setup needed
166|- **Notion URL** — via Notion MCP connector
167|- **Jira/Atlassian URL** — via Atlassian MCP connector
168|- **Linear URL** — via Linear MCP connector
169|- **Google Drive / Confluence** — via available connectors
170|- **Plain description** — describe the feature in natural language
171|
172|**Rule:** If a connector is not available, Autoframe always falls back gracefully to "paste your requirements here." It never breaks, never errors, never blocks the user.
173|
174|Text input is the default. Connectors are power-user enhancements, not gates.
175|
176|---
177|
178|## Skill Coverage by Persona
179|
180|| Skill | Persona 1 | Persona 2 | Persona 3 | Persona 4 |
181||---|---|---|---|---|
182|| `/setup` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
183|| `/new-page` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | |
184|| `/new-spec` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | |
185|| `/tc-to-spec` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
186|| `/flake-check` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | |
187|| `/coverage-map` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
188|| `/bug-from-failure` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | |
189|| `/explain` | ✅ | | | |
190|| `/refactor` | | ✅ | | |
191|| `/review-spec` | | ✅ | ✅ | |
192|| `/report` | | | | ✅ |
193|| `/new-api-spec` | | ✅ | ✅ | |
194|| `/api-coverage` | | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
195|| `/load-k6` | | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
196|
197|---
198|
199|## Positioning
200|
201|**What Autoframe is not:**
202|- Not a template (it generates frameworks, it does not just provide one)
203|- Not a single-type framework (functional + API + load in one place)
204|- Not a tool for one persona (serves manual QA, automation engineers, developers, and business equally)
205|- Not opinionated about your product (works with any web app)
206|
207|**What makes Autoframe different:**
208|- The only Playwright framework with AI skills baked in that understand its own conventions
209|- Covers functional, API, and load testing natively without separate tooling
210|- Universal input layer (text, URL, connectors) with no setup friction
211|- Built by a QA engineer, for QA engineers — not a developer side project
212|
213|---
214|
215|## Build Strategy
216|
217|**Current status:** Design docs complete. Ready to scaffold.
218|
219|**Phase 1: Foundation (Claude Code)**
220|- [x] Write AUTOFRAME.md
221|- [x] Write CLAUDE.md
222|- [ ] Create GitHub repo `github.com/kint4/autoframe`
223|- [ ] Scaffold full folder structure
224|- [ ] Wire Playwright + TypeScript + k6 baseline
225|- [ ] Set up Allure Report
226|- [ ] Set up three GitHub Actions workflows (e2e, api, load)
227|- [ ] Build all 14 skill markdown files in `.claude/skills/`
228|
229|**Phase 2: Iteration (VS Code Claude Extension)**
230|- [ ] Test each skill against a real app (automationexercise.com)
231|- [ ] Refine skill instructions based on output quality
232|- [ ] Fix conventions that do not generate correctly
233|- [ ] Dogfood as Persona 1 — if it confuses you, it will confuse them
234|
235|**Phase 3: Validation (Both)**
236|- [ ] Clone fresh repo, run `/setup`, verify end to end
237|- [ ] Use Claude Code to audit the whole project
238|- [ ] Write README with one-command quick start
239|- [ ] Record demo GIF or screenshot
240|- [ ] Publish and share
241|
242|---
243|
244|## Definition of Done
245|
246|Autoframe is ready to ship when:
247|
248|- [ ] `/setup` produces a working, runnable Playwright project from scratch
249|- [ ] All 14 skills generate correct, convention-following output
250|- [ ] Functional + API + load testing are all wired and working
251|- [ ] GitHub Actions CI/CD runs on every push
252|- [ ] README has a one-command quick start
253|- [ ] README has a demo GIF or screenshot
254|- [ ] A real case study exists (Autoframe used on an actual app)
255|- [ ] CLAUDE.md teaches Claude all Autoframe conventions correctly
256|
257|---
258|
259|## Naming
260|
261|**Autoframe** — auto implies AI-assisted generation, frame implies structure and foundation. Together: a framework that builds itself.
262|
263|Repository: `github.com/kint4/autoframe`
264|
265|---

{"content": "1|# Contributing to Autoframe
2|
3|Thanks for considering a contribution. Autoframe has two layers, and most contributions fall into one of them:
4|
5|1. **The framework** (Playwright, TypeScript, k6, fixtures, CI). Tool-agnostic code.
6|2. **The AI skill layer** (`.claude/skills/` and `CLAUDE.md`). The commands that generate code for you.
7|
8|Both are fair game. The most-wanted contribution right now is **support for other AI tools** (see below).
9|
10|## Local setup
11|
12|```bash
13|git clone https://github.com/kint4/autoframe.git
14|cd autoframe
15|npm install
16|npx playwright install
17|cp .env.example .env   # then fill in values for the app you test against
18|```
19|
20|## Running the suite
21|
22|```bash
23|npm test          # everything
24|npm run test:e2e  # E2E only
25|npm run test:api  # API only
26|npm run test:ui   # Playwright UI runner
27|npm run report    # generate and open the Allure report
28|```
29|
30|Before opening a pull request, please make sure:
31|
32|- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes (no type errors)
33|- `npm test` passes, or you have explained which tests need an environment you do not have
34|- Any new test follows the conventions in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)
35|
36|## Conventions
37|
38|[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) is the single source of truth for how code in this repo is structured: Page Object Model, spec layout, API tests, k6 scripts, naming, and folder placement. Read it before adding code. If a change would contradict CLAUDE.md, update CLAUDE.md in the same pull request and explain why.
39|
40|Quick reminders:
41|
42|- TypeScript everywhere, except k6 scripts which are JavaScript
43|- Prefer semantic locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`) over CSS selectors
44|- Never hardcode URLs, credentials, or tokens. Use environment variables
45|- Never commit a real `.env`
46|
47|## Adding or editing a skill
48|
49|Each skill is a folder under `.claude/skills/` containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter:
50|
51|```
52|.claude/skills/your-skill/SKILL.md
53|```
54|
55|```markdown
56|---
57|name: your-skill
58|description: One line that tells Claude Code when to trigger this skill.
59|---
60|
61|# /your-skill: Title
62|
63|Instructions for the skill: input format, output format, step by step.
64|```
65|
66|Two things that have bitten us before, so please check them:
67|
68|- **Do not use a flat `.md` file** directly in `.claude/skills/`. Claude Code only registers the `folder/SKILL.md` layout.
69|- **Do not name a skill after a Claude Code built-in** (for example `init`). Built-ins win the name and your skill never fires. This is why the setup command is `/setup`, not `/init`.
70|
71|Validate a new skill by typing its command in a fresh Claude Code session, not by reading the file yourself. Registration and naming bugs only show up on the real invocation path.
72|
73|## Adding support for other AI tools
74|
75|The framework works with any assistant, but the command layer is wired for Claude Code today. Porting it to another tool is the highest-value contribution available:
76|
77|- **Codex**: translate `CLAUDE.md` into an `AGENTS.md`, and adapt the skills into Codex's prompt or command format.
78|- **Cursor**: translate the conventions into `.cursor/rules`, and adapt the skills similarly.
79|- Any other LLM workflow is welcome too.
80|
81|Keep these tool-specific configs additive. The Claude Code layer should keep working alongside them.
82|
83|## Pull requests
84|
85|- Branch from `main`, keep the change focused on one thing
86|- Write a clear description of what changed and why
87|- Reference any issue it closes
88|- Small, reviewable pull requests get merged faster than large ones
89|
90|## Reporting bugs and ideas
91|
92|Open an issue. For a bug, include what you ran, what you expected, and what happened. For a feature or a new skill, describe the use case and which of the four user types (manual QA, automation engineer, developer, stakeholder) it helps.

{"content": "1|---
2|name: setup
3|description: Bootstrap the Autoframe framework for a specific product: asks about the app, then wires a ready-to-run Playwright suite. Use when the user runs /setup, asks to set up or initialize Autoframe, or wants to start a test suite for their app.
4|---
5|
6|# /setup — Bootstrap the Autoframe Project
7|
8|**Type:** Setup
9|**Description:** Bootstraps the entire Autoframe framework for a specific product. Asks for the app URL, auth type, stack details, and CI platform, then produces a fully wired, ready-to-run Playwright project. Includes a simple mode for non-technical users.
10|
11|---
12|
13|## Input Format
14|
15|The user runs `/setup`. Gather the following before generating anything:
16|
17|1. **App URL** — the base URL of the product under test (`BASE_URL`)
18|2. **API URL** — base URL for API tests, if any (`API_URL`)
19|3. **Auth type** — none / form login / token / SSO
20|4. **First feature to cover** — e.g. `auth`, `checkout`
21|5. **CI platform** — defaults to GitHub Actions
22|
23|If the user signals they are non-technical (Persona 1 or 4), switch to **simple mode**: ask only for the app URL and what they want to test first, and explain each step in plain language.
24|
25|## Output Format
26|
27|A fully scaffolded project that matches the folder structure in CLAUDE.md, with:
28|- `playwright.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`
29|- `.env.example` populated with the discovered variables
30|- `.gitignore`
31|- The three GitHub Actions workflows (`e2e.yml`, `api.yml`, `load.yml`)
32|- One starter Page Object, spec, and fixture for the first feature
33|- A short summary of what was created and how to run it
34|
35|## Step-by-Step Instructions
36|
37|1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AUTOFRAME.md` completely.
38|2. Detect the persona from the user's language (see CLAUDE.md). Adjust tone and depth.
39|3. Ask the clarifying questions above (max 3 at a time). In simple mode, ask the minimum.
40|4. Verify the folder structure exists; create any missing directories exactly as defined in CLAUDE.md.
41|5. Generate or confirm the baseline config files. Never substitute the stack.
42|6. Write `.env.example` with every required variable (`BASE_URL`, `API_URL`, `API_TOKEN`, `TEST_USER_EMAIL`, `TEST_USER_PASSWORD`). Never write a real `.env`.
43|7. Generate a starter Page Object + spec + fixture for the first feature, following the POM and spec conventions exactly.
44|8. Confirm the three CI workflows exist.
45|9. Summarize what was created and give the exact commands to install and run (`npm install`, `npx playwright install`, `npm test`).
46|10. Suggest the next skill to run (usually `/new-page` or `/tc-to-spec`).
47|
48|## Rules
49|
50|- Never deviate from the CLAUDE.md folder structure or stack.
51|- Never commit secrets; only ever write `.env.example`.
52|- In simple mode, never show config internals unless asked — explain outcomes.

{"content": "1|---
2|name: new-spec
3|description: Generate an E2E spec file with happy path, negative, and edge cases pre-written. Use when the user runs /new-spec or asks for tests for a feature or page.
4|---
5|
6|# /new-spec — Generate a Spec File
7|
8|**Type:** Functional
9|**Description:** Generates a Playwright spec file for a given feature or Page Object, with happy path, negative, and edge cases pre-written following Autoframe conventions.
10|
11|---
12|
13|## Input Format
14|
15|The user provides one of:
16|- A feature name (e.g. `login`)
17|- An existing Page Object to test
18|- A short description of the user flow
19|
20|## Output Format
21|
22|A spec file at `tests/e2e/[feature-name]/[feature].spec.ts` that follows the spec conventions in CLAUDE.md:
23|- Imports from the matching custom fixture when one exists; otherwise raw `page` with a `TODO: create fixture` comment
24|- `test.describe` grouping: Happy Path, Negative Cases, Edge Cases
25|- Arrange / Act / Assert comments in every test
26|- Test names written in plain language
27|
28|## Step-by-Step Instructions
29|
30|1. Read the spec conventions in CLAUDE.md.
31|2. Locate the relevant Page Object under `pages/[feature-name]/`. If none exists, recommend `/new-page` first.
32|3. Check `fixtures/` for a matching fixture. Use it if present; otherwise fall back to raw `page` and add the `TODO` comment.
33|4. Write the spec:
34|   - `test.describe('[Feature Name]')` as the outer block.
35|   - `beforeEach` for setup (navigate / reset state), `afterEach` for cleanup if needed.
36|   - If Negative or Edge cases need *different* setup than the Happy Path (e.g. an
37|     unauthenticated-access test must skip the login that other tests need), put the
38|     `beforeEach` inside each inner `describe` block instead of at the top level.
39|   - Inner `test.describe` blocks for Happy Path, Negative Cases, Edge Cases.
40|   - At least one meaningful test per group; never leave a group empty.
41|   - Arrange / Act / Assert comments in each test body.
42|   - Plain-language test names a non-technical person can read.
43|5. Save to `tests/e2e/[feature-name]/[feature].spec.ts`.
44|6. Suggest `/review-spec` to validate assertion quality.
45|
46|## Rules
47|
48|- No logic inside `test.describe` blocks — only inside `test` blocks.
49|- Always use Arrange / Act / Assert.
50|- Prefer custom fixtures over raw `page` whenever a fixture exists.
51|- Drive the page through Page Object methods, not raw locators in the spec.

35|7. Offer to explain a related file next.

37|## Rules
38|
39|- Teach the pattern, not just the syntax.

{"content": "1|---
2|name: load-k6
3|description: Generate a k6 load test script with ramp-up stages and pass/fail thresholds. Use when the user runs /load-k6 or asks for a load or performance test.
4|---
5|
6|# /load-k6 — Generate a k6 Load Test
7|
8|**Type:** Load
9|**Description:** Generates a k6 load test script for a described scenario, with real ramp-up/sustain/ramp-down stages, thresholds, and a readable report.
10|
11|---
12|
13|## Input Format
14|
15|The user describes the scenario:
16|- The endpoint or flow to load test
17|- Expected/target traffic (concurrent users)
18|- Performance goals (acceptable latency, error rate)
19|
20|If targets aren't given, use Autoframe defaults: 50 ramp-up → 100 sustained, p95 < 500ms, error rate < 1%.
21|
22|## Output Format
23|
24|A k6 script at `performance/load/[scenario].load.js` following the k6 conventions in CLAUDE.md:
25|- `options.stages`: ramp up, sustained load, ramp down — **real numbers, never placeholders**
26|- `options.thresholds`: p95 response time and error rate
27|- `__ENV.BASE_URL` for the base URL — never hardcoded
28|- `check()` assertions and a `sleep()` per iteration
29|
30|## Step-by-Step Instructions
31|
32|1. Read the k6 conventions in CLAUDE.md.
33|2. **Confirm the target URL is not production.** If it is, require explicit user confirmation before generating or running.
34|3. **Check the target path is HTTP-reachable.** Single-page apps route paths like
35|   `/inventory.html` client-side — a raw `http.get` to them returns 404. For SPAs,
36|   target the document root or real API endpoints instead. Verify with one request
37|   (`curl -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`) before generating the script.
38|4. Translate the scenario into concrete stages and thresholds (use defaults if unspecified).
39|5. Write the script:
40|   - `import http from 'k6/http'` and `{ check, sleep } from 'k6'`.
41|   - `export const options` with `stages` (real durations/targets) and `thresholds`.
42|   - `export default function ()` that hits `${__ENV.BASE_URL}/[path]`, runs `check()`s, and `sleep(1)`.
43|6. Use kebab-case + `.load.js` suffix.
44|7. Save to `performance/load/[scenario].load.js`.
45|8. Tell the user how to run it: `BASE_URL=... k6 run performance/load/[scenario].load.js` (or via the `load.yml` workflow).
46|
47|## Rules
48|
49|- Never use placeholder text like `[ramp-up]` in stage targets — always real numbers.
50|- Always use `__ENV.BASE_URL`; never hardcode URLs.
51|- Always define ramp up, sustained, ramp down stages and both thresholds.
52|- Never run against production without explicit user confirmation.
53|- k6 scripts are JavaScript (the one exception to the TypeScript rule).

29|          echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/k6-archive-keyring.gpg] https://dl.k6.io/deb stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/k6.list
30|          sudo apt-get update

messages.content:
{"content": "1|---
2|name: tc-to-spec
3|description: Convert requirements (pasted text, Notion, Jira, or Linear link) into a runnable Playwright spec. Use when the user runs /tc-to-spec or provides requirements to turn into tests.
4|---
5|
6|# /tc-to-spec — Requirements to Spec
7|
8|**Type:** Functional
9|**Description:** Takes requirements from any source (pasted text, Notion, Jira, Linear, Confluence, or a plain description) and generates a runnable Playwright spec file.
10|
11|---
12|
13|## Input Format
14|
15|Any of:
16|- Pasted plain-text requirements or acceptance criteria
17|- A Notion / Jira / Linear / Confluence URL (fetched via the available MCP connector)
18|- A natural-language feature description
19|
20|If the input is a URL and no connector is available, say: "I don't have access to that connector. Please paste the requirements directly here and I'll generate from that." For `.pdf` / `.docx` / `.csv`, ask the user to paste the relevant content.
21|
22|## Output Format
23|
24|A spec file at `tests/e2e/[feature-name]/[feature].spec.ts` following the spec conventions in CLAUDE.md, with each requirement mapped to one or more tests across Happy Path, Negative Cases, and Edge Cases.
25|
26|## Step-by-Step Instructions
27|
28|1. Read the spec conventions in CLAUDE.md.
29|2. Acquire the requirements:
30|   - Plain text → use directly.
31|   - URL → fetch via the matching connector; fall back to "paste here" if unavailable.
32|   - Description → ask up to 3 clarifying questions before generating.
33|   - Binary file → ask the user to paste the content.
34|3. Extract discrete, testable acceptance criteria. List them back to the user for confirmation if ambiguous.
35|4. Map each criterion to a test and classify it as Happy Path, Negative, or Edge.
36|5. Check for an existing Page Object and fixture for the feature; if missing, recommend `/new-page` and use raw `page` with a `TODO` comment in the meantime.
37|6. Generate the spec following all spec conventions (describe grouping, AAA comments, plain-language names).
38|7. Save to `tests/e2e/[feature-name]/[feature].spec.ts`.
39|8. Show a short traceability summary mapping each requirement to its test name.
40|
41|## Rules
42|
43|- Never block on a missing connector — always fall back to paste.
44|- Every requirement must map to at least one test.
45|- Follow the spec conventions exactly.
46|", "total_lines": 45, "file_size": 2300, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

{"content": "1|---
2|name: coverage-map
3|description: Map spec files against requirements or features to show what is covered, missing, and redundant. Use when the user runs /coverage-map or asks what is tested.
4|---
5|
6|# /coverage-map — Map Test Coverage
7|
8|**Type:** Functional
9|**Description:** Reads all spec files and maps them against requirements or features, showing what is covered, what is missing, and what is redundant.
10|
11|---
12|
13|## Input Format
14|
15|Optional:
16|- A list of requirements / features (pasted or via connector)
17|- A feature name to scope the report
18|
19|With no input, map all existing E2E specs by feature folder.
20|
21|## Output Format
22|
23|A coverage table grouped by feature:
24|
25|| Feature | Covered | Missing | Redundant |
26||---|---|---|---|
27|
28|Plus a short prose summary and a prioritized list of gaps to close (with the suggested skill for each).
29|
30|## Step-by-Step Instructions
31|
32|1. Enumerate every spec under `tests/e2e/` (and the feature folders).
33|2. Parse each spec's `test.describe` and `test` names to build the list of covered behaviors.
34|3. If requirements were provided, align covered behaviors to each requirement; otherwise infer expected coverage from the feature and existing Page Objects.
35|4. Identify:
36|   - **Covered** — requirement has at least one passing-shaped test.
37|   - **Missing** — requirement with no matching test.
38|   - **Redundant** — multiple tests asserting the same behavior with no added value.
39|5. Render the coverage table grouped by feature.
40|6. Give a prioritized gap list, recommending `/tc-to-spec` or `/new-spec` to close each gap.
41|7. For stakeholder-facing summaries, point to `/report`.
42|
43|## Rules
44|
45|- Read specs, never execute them, to build the map.
46|- Be explicit about assumptions when requirements are not provided.
47|- Group everything by feature to match the folder structure.
48|", "total_lines": 47, "file_size": 1845, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

Saya sudah pelajari repo `kint4/autoframe`.

## Inti repo ini

**Autoframe** adalah **starter framework QA automation** yang dibungkus dengan **layer AI untuk generate test**.  
Fokusnya: bikin tim bisa cepat punya suite testing yang rapi untuk:

- **E2E testing** pakai **Playwright**
- **API testing** pakai **Playwright request**
- **Load testing** pakai **k6**
- **Reporting** pakai **Allure**
- **CI/CD** pakai **GitHub Actions**

Jadi ini **bukan app biasa**, dan juga **bukan library runtime yang kompleks**.  
Lebih tepatnya: **template + aturan arsitektur + kumpulan prompt/skill AI** supaya test suite bisa dibangun dan dikembangkan dengan pola yang konsisten.

---

## Cara berpikir repo ini

Repo ini punya **2 lapisan utama**:

### 1. Lapisan framework teknis
Ini bagian “kode/framework”-nya:

- `playwright.config.ts`
- `package.json`
- `tsconfig.json`
- `.github/workflows/*.yml`
- `utils/*`
- `performance/load/example.load.js`

Bagian ini menentukan:
- cara test dijalankan
- browser/project mana yang dipakai
- struktur folder
- env vars
- reporting
- CI pipeline

### 2. Lapisan AI assistant
Ini bagian yang paling unik:

- `CLAUDE.md`
- `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`

Layer ini berisi **instruksi dan slash-command untuk Claude Code**, misalnya:

- `/setup`
- `/new-spec`
- `/new-page`
- `/tc-to-spec`
- `/review-spec`
- `/coverage-map`
- `/new-api-spec`
- `/load-k6`
- `/report`
- dll

Artinya, “AI built in” di sini **bukan berarti ada backend AI custom di repo**, tapi **repo ini menanamkan prompt conventions + skill files** yang dipakai Claude Code untuk bantu generate test.

---

## Struktur repo yang penting

### Folder utama
- `tests/e2e/` → test E2E per fitur
- `tests/api/` → test API per fitur
- `pages/` → Page Object Model
- `fixtures/` → custom fixture Playwright
- `data/factories/` → generator data test
- `data/seeds/` → seed data
- `performance/load/` → skrip k6
- `utils/` → helper umum
- `.claude/skills/` → skill AI
- `.github/workflows/` → pipeline CI

### Observasi penting
Saat saya inspect repo hasil clone, banyak folder masih berisi **`.gitkeep` saja**:

- `tests/e2e/*`
- `tests/api/*`
- `pages/*`
- `fixtures/`
- `data/*`

Jadi repo publik ini sekarang lebih terasa sebagai **framework skeleton / factory**, bukan contoh project yang sudah penuh test nyata.

---

## Stack yang dipakai

Dari `package.json` dan config:

- **Playwright** → `@playwright/test`
- **TypeScript**
- **Allure Playwright**
- **dotenv**
- **Faker.js**
- **k6** untuk load testing

Script penting:
- `npm test`
- `npm run test:e2e`
- `npm run test:api`
- `npm run report`
- `npm run load`

---

## Cara kerja teknisnya

### Playwright config
`playwright.config.ts` cukup rapi. Beberapa poin bagus:

- `testDir: './tests'`
- memisahkan browser projects:
  - `chromium`
  - `firefox`
  - `webkit`
- ada project khusus:
  - `api`

Hal penting:
- file `*.api.spec.ts` **di-ignore di browser projects**
- lalu dijalankan khusus di project `api`

Ini desain yang bagus, karena mencegah **API test ikut kebawa ke run browser**.

---

## Filosofi testing-nya

Repo ini sangat opinionated.  
Di `CLAUDE.md`, mereka memaksa pola berikut:

### Untuk E2E
- **Page Object Model**
- locator semantik (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`, dst)
- test dikelompokkan:
  - Happy Path
  - Negative Cases
  - Edge Cases
- format test pakai komentar:
  - Arrange
  - Act
  - Assert

### Untuk API test
- selalu cek:
  - status code
  - response schema
  - auth failure
  - invalid input

### Untuk load test
- wajib ada:
  - ramp up
  - sustain
  - ramp down
  - threshold latency
  - threshold error rate

Jadi repo ini bukan sekadar “tempat taruh test”, tapi **opinionated methodology**.

---

## Yang paling menarik dari repo ini

### 1. Nilai utamanya ada di **AI workflow**, bukan di business logic
Kalau dilihat dari kode mentah, isi runtime repo ini sebenarnya masih ringan:
- helper kecil
- constants env
- satu contoh k6 script
- config + workflow

**Nilai besarnya justru di:**
- konvensi
- struktur
- skill AI
- guidance untuk generate test

### 2. Claude Code jadi “engine”
Semua command seperti `/setup`, `/new-spec`, `/tc-to-spec` sebenarnya hidup di file markdown skill.  
Jadi pengalaman user yang diincar adalah:

1. clone repo
2. buka di Claude Code
3. panggil command
4. AI generate suite sesuai aturan Autoframe

### 3. Repo ini lebih mirip “framework factory”
Mereka sendiri mendeskripsikannya begitu.  
Artinya: bukan template statis, tapi **basis yang dibesarkan oleh AI seiring produk berkembang**.

---

## 14 skill AI yang saya temukan

Ada 14 skill di `.claude/skills/`, termasuk:

- `setup`
- `new-page`
- `new-spec`
- `tc-to-spec`
- `flake-check`
- `coverage-map`
- `bug-from-failure`
- `explain`
- `refactor`
- `review-spec`
- `report`
- `new-api-spec`
- `api-coverage`
- `load-k6`

Secara produk, ini masuk akal: mereka mencoba cover lifecycle QA dari:
- setup awal
- generate test
- review kualitas
- coverage
- bug reporting
- load testing
- reporting ke stakeholder

---

## Kelebihan repo ini

### Bagus untuk:
- tim QA yang baru mulai automation
- developer yang butuh test framework cepat
- tim kecil yang ingin satu repo untuk E2E + API + load
- workflow AI-assisted test generation

### Nilai plus:
- struktur jelas
- opinionated, jadi tidak bikin bingung
- CI sudah disiapkan
- command AI cukup lengkap
- memisahkan test type dengan rapi
- aman soal secret: pakai `.env`, tidak hardcode

---

## Kekurangan / catatan kritis

### 1. Repo publiknya masih sangat skeleton
Saat saya cek:
- belum ada spec `.spec.ts` nyata
- belum ada page object nyata
- fixture juga belum ada isi

Jadi kalau orang berharap “langsung lihat contoh suite yang matang”, repo ini belum terlalu kaya contoh.

### 2. Sangat bergantung ke Claude Code untuk pengalaman terbaik
README juga jujur soal ini:
- framework-nya bisa dipakai siapa saja
- tapi **slash command-nya wired ke Claude Code**

Jadi kalau user pakai tool lain, perlu port manual.

### 3. Ada sedikit indikasi doc drift
`AUTOFRAME.md` masih punya bagian “build strategy” yang terdengar seperti repo ini sedang menuju scaffold penuh, padahal sekarang repo dan strukturnya sudah ada.  
Bukan masalah besar, tapi tanda bahwa sebagian dokumen design masih campur antara **vision doc** dan **current state**.

### 4. “AI-native” di sini lebih ke prompt architecture
Kalau orang membaca sekilas, bisa salah paham mengira ada agent runtime / backend orchestration di kode.  
Padahal realitanya: **AI layer = instruction files + skill markdown**.

---

## Kesimpulan singkat

Kalau saya sederhanakan:

> **Autoframe adalah starter kit QA automation yang sangat opinionated, dengan Playwright + TypeScript + k6 + Allure + GitHub Actions, lalu ditambah layer prompt/skill untuk Claude Code agar test bisa di-generate, direview, dan dikelola lebih cepat.**

### Dalam praktiknya, repo ini:
- **kuat sebagai fondasi**
- **kuat sebagai sistem konvensi**
- **kuat sebagai AI-assisted workflow**
- tapi **belum kaya contoh implementasi nyata di repo publiknya**

Jadi ini cocok kalau tujuanmu adalah:
- mempercepat bootstrap automation
- menjaga struktur suite tetap rapi
- pakai AI untuk bantu generate test

Kurang cocok kalau tujuanmu adalah:
- mencari repo contoh dengan banyak test riil siap dipelajari langsung

---

Kalau mau, next saya bisa bantu salah satu dari ini:

1. **bedah struktur folder satu per satu**,  
2. **jelaskan cara kerja skill AI-nya lebih dalam**, atau  
3. **review apakah repo ini bagus dipakai untuk timmu / dibanding framework lain**.

# PRDanalisis Role Workflow

Use this skill when working in the `PRDanalisis` workspace on tasks that involve more than one of these concerns:
- draft or update a PRD
- analyze requirements, dependencies, or risks
- prepare QA review, testcase strategy, or automation mapping
- implement automation/code after requirements are stabilized
- coordinate reviewer approvals across stages

This skill captures the user's preferred **role-based orchestration**, not just a generic analysis sequence.

## Core principle

Treat the work as a **gated requirement-delivery workflow**, not as one long freeform task.

The normal full-lane sequence is:
1. Orchestrator classifies the task and chooses a lane
2. Draft PRD v0 / PRD skeleton is created
3. Analyst produces the **Assessment Report**
4. Reviewer performs **early review** on assessment + PRD draft
5. PRD Writer updates the PRD to requirement-ready
6. QA Agent performs **pre-implementation QA review**
7. Reviewer approves and **freezes the requirement package**
8. Coder implements (often automation code / automation repo changes)
9. QA Agent performs **post-implementation validation**
10. Reviewer performs final review and sign-off

## Naming and ownership rules

### Analyst-owned artifact name
If the owner is Analyst, do **not** call the main artifact "QA Assessment Report".
Use:
- `Assessment Report`, or
- `Analyst Assessment Report`

Default to **Assessment Report**.

Reason: ownership must stay clear.
- Analyst owns assessment, dependency mapping, risk baseline, and impact baseline
- QA owns QA review, regression/test impact, coverage strategy, and automation mapping

## Lane selection

### Full Lane
Use the full workflow for:
- new features
- new PRDs
- major PRD patches
- behavior-sensitive automation changes
- cross-domain or high-dependency work

### Fast Lane
Use the shortened workflow for:
- small automation-only changes
- narrow testcase patches
- minor PRD wording changes
- bug fixes with small and well-bounded impact

Fast lane:
1. Orchestrator
2. Quick Assessment (Analyst and/or QA)
3. Reviewer quick approve
4. Coder
5. QA
6. Reviewer final

## Stage guidance

### Stage 2 — Draft PRD v0
The first draft is a **skeleton**, not a final PRD.
Minimum content:
- problem statement
- objective
- scope / non-scope
- actor or user role
- main flow
- assumptions
- open questions

Do **not** over-invest in detailed acceptance/test assets before assessment and early review.

### Stage 3 — Analyst checklist
Analyst must always check at least:
- lifecycle / state impact
- SLA impact
- RBAC / permission impact
- dependency impact
- backward compatibility
- edge-case / exception behavior

### Stage 6 — QA pre-implementation scope
Before coding, QA focuses on:
- PRD review
- QA impact / regression analysis
- requirement coverage matrix
- testcase outline / strategy
- automation candidate mapping
- blocker or mismatch notes

Do **not** force QA to finalize post-implementation validation artifacts at this stage.

### Stage 9 — QA post-implementation scope
After coding, QA focuses on:
- regression result
- automation alignment validation
- coverage confirmation
- uncovered gaps
- defect / mismatch notes

Keep pre-implementation and post-implementation QA outputs separate.

## Requirement Package Freeze

After reviewer approval at Gate B, treat the package as frozen input for implementation.

The **Requirement Package** includes:
- PRD
- Assessment Report
- QA review
- coverage / testcase strategy
- automation scope

### Pitfall: silent mid-implementation requirement drift
Do **not** let coding continue silently if requirements change after Gate B.
If a requirement changes after freeze:
1. send the change back to the requirement lane
2. perform at least a delta review
3. re-approve before continuing implementation

This rule is especially important for automation work, where mapping, testcase scope, and expected behavior often drift mid-stream.

## Reviewer decision schemas

Reviewer output should be machine-routable, not only narrative.

### Gate A — Early Review
Use exactly one:
- `APPROVE_WITH_NOTES`
- `REVISE_ASSESSMENT`
- `REVISE_PRD_DRAFT`
- `HOLD`

### Gate B — Requirement Package Approval
Use exactly one:
- `APPROVED`
- `APPROVED_WITH_CAUTION`
- `REVISE_PRD`
- `HOLD`

### Gate C — Final Review
Use exactly one:
- `FINAL_APPROVE`
- `REVISE_CODER`
- `REVISE_QA`
- `REOPEN_REQUIREMENT`

## Relationship to repo rules

This skill does **not** replace repository rules. It sits on top of them.
Always still follow:
- `Rules/agent-instruction.md`
- `Rules/workflow-rule.md`
- task-type rules (`qa-analysis-rule.md`, `prd-writing-rule.md`, `test-case-rule.md`, `impact-analysis-rule.md`, `automation-bridge-rule.md`)
- `Memory/global-memory.md` and relevant feature memory

## Artifact expectations by role

- Orchestrator → task brief, lane selection, role routing
- Analyst → Assessment Report
- PRD Writer → PRD v0 or requirement-ready PRD
- QA Agent (pre) → QA review, regression/test impact, coverage strategy, automation candidate mapping
- Coder → implementation and deviation notes if needed
- QA Agent (post) → regression result, automation alignment validation, uncovered gap/defect note
- Reviewer → gate decision and sign-off

# PRDanalisis QA Browser

## When to load this skill
Load this skill when the user asks to inspect, modify, troubleshoot, or design behavior for the PRDanalisis QA Browser stack:
- `Test/testcase-browser.html`
- `server.js`
- `Scripts/gdocs.js`
- `Scripts/mirror.js`
- sidebar file tree / virtual sections
- Google Docs / Google Drive integration
- local PRD/Test/BRD file creation or import/export flows

This is especially relevant for requests like:
- "QA browser / testcase-browser.html"
- "Google Docs connect / import / export / mirror"
- "show only one Google Drive folder"
- "import docs back into PRDanalisis"

## First reads
Before answering or changing code, inspect these repo files first:
1. `Memory/qa-tooling.md` — current documented behavior of QA Browser and server endpoints.
2. `GDOCS-SETUP.md` — OAuth setup and root-folder config.
3. `Test/testcase-browser.html` — frontend wiring.
4. `server.js` — REST endpoints and local file write primitives.
5. `Scripts/gdocs.js` — Drive tree listing, Doc→Markdown, Markdown→Doc behavior.
6. `Scripts/mirror.js` — current one-way local→Google mirror.

## Current Google Docs architecture to assume unless code proves otherwise
### Frontend
- Google Docs appears as a **virtual sidebar section**, merged into `allSections`.
- `loadGDocs()` fetches `/api/gdocs/status` and, when connected, `/api/gdocs`.
- Opening a Google Doc fetches `/api/gdocs/:id` and renders the result as **read-only markdown**.
- Markdown files can be exported to a **new Google Doc** via `POST /api/gdocs` from `MarkdownViewer`.

### Backend
- `server.js` exposes OAuth endpoints:
  - `/api/google/status`
  - `/api/google/login`
  - `/oauth2callback`
  - `/api/google/logout`
- Docs endpoints:
  - `GET /api/gdocs` — tree/list view
  - `POST /api/gdocs` — create new doc
  - `GET /api/gdocs/:id` — read doc as markdown
  - `PUT /api/gdocs/:id` — update doc
- Mirror endpoint:
  - `POST /api/mirror` — pushes local `PRD/*.md` to Google Docs
- Local write primitives already exist:
  - `PUT /api/files/content`
  - `POST /api/files/mkdir`

### Drive scoping behavior
`Scripts/gdocs.js` already supports a **single root folder scope**:
- If `GDRIVE_FOLDER_ID` is set, list from that folder.
- Else if `GDRIVE_FOLDER_NAME` is set, resolve that folder and list from it.
- Else fallback is **all Google Docs in Drive** as a flat list.

So if the user says "sekarang tampil semua docs", first suspect **root folder config is not set**, not that the feature is impossible.

## Working rules for Google Docs requests
### 1) "Show only one folder"
Treat this as two different asks:
- **Config-only scoping**: already supported via `GDRIVE_FOLDER_ID` / `GDRIVE_FOLDER_NAME`.
- **Runtime folder picker in UI**: new feature; requires extra API + frontend selection state.

Always explain which one the user means or, if they ask for feasibility, explain both.

### 2) "Import from Google Docs back into PRDanalisis"
Do **not** describe this as existing behavior unless you verify code says so.
Current baseline is:
- read Google Docs in sidebar
- export local markdown to Google Docs
- mirror local `PRD/*.md` to Google Docs

A true reverse flow (Google→local) is a **new feature**.

## Recommended design pattern for reverse import
Prefer a **manual one-way import** first, not bi-directional sync.

### Suggested v1
1. User selects or configures one Google Drive root folder.
2. App lists only that folder tree.
3. User triggers `Import folder to PRDanalisis`.
4. Backend recursively walks Drive folders and docs.
5. Each Google Doc is converted to markdown.
6. Local folders are created to mirror the Drive tree.
7. Files are written under the local target (usually `PRD/`).
8. Sidebar refreshes and optional `/api/import` reindex runs.

### Default mapping rule
If the chosen Drive folder is the import root, map its children directly under local `PRD/` unless product rules say otherwise.

Example:
- Drive root: `SatuInbox PRD/Conversationv2/...`
- Local result: `PRD/Conversationv2/...`

## Important pitfalls
- Distinguish **folder structure fidelity** from **document formatting fidelity**.
  - Folder structure can be mirrored closely.
  - Document formatting is only partially preserved by the current Doc→Markdown converter.
- The current converter is suitable for headings, bullets, bold, italic, links, and simple tables; complex Docs features are not guaranteed.
- Avoid jumping straight to two-way sync; start with manual import and explicit conflict handling.
- If overwrite risk exists, recommend preview/dry-run and conflict policy (`skip`, `overwrite`, `rename copy`).
- Google Drive can contain duplicate names that map badly to local filesystems; plan for collision handling.

## Verification checklist before you finalize advice
- Confirm whether folder scoping is already possible through env/config.
- Confirm whether import-to-local actually exists or is only proposed.
- State exactly which files/endpoints would change for implementation.
- If discussing structure preservation, separate:
  - tree structure preservation
  - markdown/content fidelity limits

## Useful support files
- `references/google-docs-integration.md` — current extracted behavior, endpoint map, and implementation notes for folder scoping + reverse import.

## Workflow Notes (Current Canonical)

- Logical nama artefak analisa permanen adalah **Assessment Report**.

{"content": "1|# Agent Instruction — Wajib Dibaca Sebelum Eksekusi
2|
3|Ini adalah **system prompt replacement**. Agent wajib mengikuti workflow ini di **setiap sesi**, tanpa terkecuali. Tidak ada tugas yang boleh dikerjakan tanpa membaca rule yang sesuai.
4|
5|---
6|
7|## Step 0: Muat Konteks Tambahan
8|
9|Selain rule, agent WAJIB tahu keberadaan:
10|
11|- **`WORKFLOW_CONTEXT.md`** — konteks onboarding lengkap: arsitektur 3-repo, automation bridge pipeline, page objects index, commands cheatsheet, environment accounts
12|- **`Memory/qa-tooling.md`** — dokumentasi testcase-browser.html (QA Browser) + server.js (QA Agent) — fitur aktif, mode, arsitektur frontend, SSE format
13|
14|## Step 1: Deteksi Tipe Tugas
15|
16|Begitu user memberi prompt, klasifikasikan ke salah satu tipe berikut:
17|
18|| Jika user bilang... | Tipe Tugas |
19||---|---|
20|| buat PRD / tulis PRD / draft PRD / create PRD / write PRD / PRD baru | PRD WRITING |
21|| analisa / analyze / review PRD / cek PRD / analisis | ANALYSIS |
22|| buat memory / tulis memory / simpan ke memory / update memory | MEMORY WRITE |
23|| bandingkan / compare / perbedaan / perbandingan | COMPARISON |
24|| test case / test scenario / test steps / test plan / QA test / regression / UAT / uji / testing | TEST CASE |
25|| bug / perbaiki bug / error / issue / defect | BUG FIX |
26|| impact / dampak / efek samping / blast radius | IMPACT ANALYSIS |
27|| feature / fitur baru /开发 | FEATURE DEV |
28|
29|Jika user memberi perintah yang tidak eksplisit (misal: "tolong review PRD ini", "cek apakah ada masalah"), tetap klasifikasikan ke tipe tugas yang paling sesuai.
30|
31|> **Jika ragu: muat SEMUA rule dari `Rules/`.**
32|
33|---
34|
35|## Step 2: Muat Rule Berdasarkan Tipe Tugas
36|
37|### Untuk SEMUA tipe tugas (wajib):
38|
39|1. `Rules/workflow-rule.md` — execution order dan prioritas
40|2. `Rules/structure-rule.md` — repository structure, termasuk lokasi artefak permanen di `Assessments/` dan script helper di `Scripts/`
41|3. `Memory/README.md` — memory index, tahu file mana yang ada dan fungsinya
42|4. `Assessments/README.md` — aturan artefak analisa permanen dan versioning bila tugas menyentuh hasil analisa yang ingin dipersist
43|
44|### ANALYSIS / PRD / FEATURE DEV:
45|
46|```
47|Rules/qa-analysis-rule.md         → WAJIB. Full methodology + Assessment Report format + decision enum.
48|Rules/impact-analysis-rule.md     → Untuk cek blast radius.
49|Assessments/templates/qa-assessment-report-template.md → Template artefak permanen assessment.
50|Assessments/templates/Setup/assessment-report-template.md → Operational wrapper untuk Assessment Report milik Analyst.
51|```
52|
53|### PRD WRITING:
54|
55|```
56|Rules/prd-writing-rule.md         → WAJIB. Template dan framework penulisan PRD.
57|Rules/qa-analysis-rule.md         → Untuk memastikan requirement testable dan lengkap.
58|Rules/impact-analysis-rule.md     → Jika PRD menyentuh flow/entity existing atau cross-feature dependency.
59|```
60|
61|### BUG FIX:
62|
63|```
64|Rules/qa-analysis-rule.md         → Type 2: Bug Fix Analysis.
65|Rules/impact-analysis-rule.md     → Blast radius dan regression.
66|```
67|
68|### IMPACT ANALYSIS:
69|
70|```
71|Rules/impact-analysis-rule.md     → WAJIB. Impact dimensions.
72|Rules/qa-analysis-rule.md         → Mandatory Impact Dimensions + Risk Analysis.
73|```
74|
75|### COMPARISON (PRD vs PRD):
76|
77|```
78|Rules/prd-comparison-rule.md      → WAJIB. Framework compare.
79|Rules/qa-analysis-rule.md         → Interconnection analysis jika PRD saling terkait.
80|```
81|
82|### TEST CASE:
83|
84|```
85|Rules/test-case-rule.md           → WAJIB. QA test writing, steps, coverage, execution support.
86|Rules/qa-analysis-rule.md         → WAJIB. Source analysis dan Test Specification Layer.
87|Rules/impact-analysis-rule.md     → Jika test perlu regression, rollout, rollback, atau cross-feature coverage.
88|Rules/automation-bridge-rule.md   → Jika test case TSV akan disinkronkan ke repo automation.
89|Assessments/templates/Setup/qa-pre-implementation-review-template.md  → Untuk QA review sebelum coding.
90|Assessments/templates/Setup/qa-post-implementation-validation-template.md → Untuk QA validation setelah coding.
91|Assessments/templates/Setup/automation-mapping-template.md → Untuk companion mapping requirement ↔ automation.
92|```
93|
94|Output test case tidak terbatas pada TSV. Jika feature belum punya generator bridge, simpan juga companion docs di `Test/<domain>/` sebagai `*-qa-test-spec.md` dan `*-automation-mapping.md`.
95|
96|### MEMORY WRITE:
97|
98|```
99|Rules/memory-routing-rule.md      → WAJIB. Tahu konten masuk global atau feature memory.
100|Rules/memory-write-rule.md        → Jika akan menulis memory baru.
101|Rules/memory-update-rule.md       → Jika akan update feature memory yang sudah ada.
102|Rules/global-memory-write-rule.md → Jika akan menulis global memory baru.
103|Rules/global-memory-update-rule.md→ Jika akan update global memory.
104|```
105|
106|---
107|
108|## Step 3: Muat Konteks Produk
109|
110|Setelah rule terbaca, muat konteks:
111|
112|1. `Memory/global-memory.md` — canonical product rules, dependency, open risks
113|2. File memory relevan dari `Memory/` — feature-specific detail
114|
115|Gunakan `Memory/README.md` untuk navigasi cepat ke file yang tepat.
116|
117|### Kapan harus muat `Memory/CLAUDE-be.md`
118|
119|Muat jika tugas menyentuh salah satu dari:
120|- Mengecek apakah fitur sudah diimplementasi di BE
121|- Impact analysis yang perlu tahu service boundary, gRPC contract, atau RabbitMQ pattern
122|- Bug fix yang butuh verifikasi schema, enum, atau data model BE
123|- Feature dev yang perlu tahu service mana yang harus diubah / proto baru
124|- Test case yang butuh cross-check BE endpoint atau event pattern
125|
126|### Kapan harus muat `Memory/CLAUDE-fe.md`
127|
128|Muat jika tugas menyentuh salah satu dari:
129|- Mengecek apakah fitur sudah diimplementasi di FE
130|- Impact analysis yang perlu tahu component tree, Zustand store, atau service hook
131|- Bug fix yang butuh verifikasi routing, state management, atau socket event FE
132|- Feature dev yang perlu tahu component mana yang harus diubah / hook baru
133|- Test case yang butuh cross-check FE component mapping atau URL routing
134|
135|---
136|
137|## Step 4: Eksekusi
138|
139|Gunakan rule yang sudah dimuat sebagai **metodologi kerja**, bukan sekadar referensi.
140|
141|- Output harus sesuai struktur yang ditentukan rule
142|- Hasil analisis yang bersifat decision-bearing harus dipermanenkan sebagai Assessment Report di `Assessments/`
143|- Jangan lewati section impact/risk/regression
144|- Jika ada kontradiksi antara input user dan rule, ikuti rule
145|
146|---
147|
148|## Aturan Kritis: Self-Triggered Actions
149|
150|Agent mungkin **dalam proses eksekusi** perlu melakukan tindakan lain tanpa diperintah eksplisit. Contoh:
151|
152|| Saat sedang... | Agent perlu... | Maka baca... |
153||---|---|---|
154|| Menganalisa PRD | Menyimpan temuan ke memory | Memory rules |
155|| Menulis PRD | Mengecek struktur, testability, dan impact | prd-writing-rule.md, qa-analysis-rule.md, impact-analysis-rule.md |
156|| Membuat QA test / steps | Menyusun coverage, traceability, execution support | test-case-rule.md, qa-analysis-rule.md |
157|| Membuat / update test case TSV | Mengikuti template `SatuInbox Test Case Scenario V2` | test-case-rule.md |
158|| Membuat test case | Merevisi analisa karena ada temuan baru | qa-analysis-rule.md |
159|| Memperbaiki bug | Mengecek dampak ke modul lain | impact-analysis-rule.md |
160|| Membandingkan PRD | Analisa interkoneksi | qa-analysis-rule.md |
161|| Menganalisa PRD / bug / impact | Verifikasi status implementasi BE | Memory/CLAUDE-be.md |
162|| Menganalisa PRD / bug / impact | Verifikasi status implementasi FE | Memory/CLAUDE-fe.md |
163|
164|**Setiap kali agent akan:**
165|- Menganalisa sesuatu → baca `qa-analysis-rule.md`
166|- Menulis PRD → baca `prd-writing-rule.md`
167|- Menulis/update file → baca memory rules
168|- Membandingkan → baca `prd-comparison-rule.md`
169|- Membuat test case → baca `test-case-rule.md`
170|- Membuat atau update test case TSV → baca `test-case-rule.md`
171|- Mengecek dampak → baca `impact-analysis-rule.md`
172|- Verifikasi implementasi BE → baca `Memory/CLAUDE-be.md`
173|- Verifikasi implementasi FE → baca `Memory/CLAUDE-fe.md`
174|
175|Tidak ada "saya sudah tahu, tidak perlu baca ulang". **Setiap tindakan = baca rule yang sesuai.**
176|
177|---
178|
179|## Ringkasan Sederhana
180|
181|```
182|Ada perintah → klasifikasi tipe tugas → muat rule sesuai tipe → muat konteks → eksekusi
183|Dalam proses → butuh lakukan hal lain → muat rule untuk hal itu → lanjut
184|```
185|
186|Jika ada 1 menit downtime karena baca rule, itu lebih baik daripada 1 hari downtime karena salah analisa.
